questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Money as exchange and as store of value
questions.learningObjective: Identify which asset best serves as a store of value under inflation
questions.stem: Maya keeps savings in cash while prices rise five percent a year; which asset better preserves purchasing power over a decade?

options.text: Rolling over short-term government bills that adjust with market rates
Buying a broad stock index fund that historically outpaces consumer prices
options.misconception: confuses liquidity with long-run real return

options.text: Holding additional currency because cash is the most liquid asset available
options.misconception: ignores erosion of purchasing power by inflation

options.text: Spending the savings immediately to avoid any future price increase

questions.explanation: Short-term bills reset to market rates and keep real value stable, while cash loses purchasing power; spending everything is not storing value at all.
questions.hint: Compare real returns, not nominal liquidity.

questions.explanation: A checking balance is immediately spendable and clears payments, so it is the medium of exchange; the others store value or earn returns.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why M2 exceeds M1 in a given economy
questions.stem: Explain why the broad money measure M2 is always larger than the narrow measure M1 in any economy with banks.

answer.exemplar: M2 equals M1 plus savings deposits and small time deposits, so every dollar in M1 is already counted and the broader measure adds non-transaction balances, making M2 larger whenever such deposits exist.

questions.explanation: M2 contains all of M1 plus additional liquid assets, so it cannot be smaller; the extra components are savings and time deposits.
questions.hint: Recall that M2 nests M1 inside it.
